title: Managed Execution, Runtime Observation and Replay
summary: After placement, a managed execution surface binds the exact target and capability generation. Runtime observations and provider receipts remain evidence; ambiguity is held for explicit reconciliation rather than automatically retried or released.
why: A provider call can outlive a transport reply, and a target can change after planning. Safe execution requires replay fencing and fresh identity checks rather than optimistic retry.
invariants: Job-to-Node network6 preserves fail-closed lifecycle recovery and does not grant runtime observation release authority.
RUNNING, ABSENT and UNKNOWN runtime observations do not release placement by themselves.
RexxOS Managed Compute MU rejects placement-target mismatch, stale target generation, job mismatch and expired lease.
A repeated request ID after a claimed provider call remains REPLAY_HELD; changed content is REQUEST_ID_CONFLICT; uncertain provider receipt is EXECUTION_UNCERTAIN.
Production managed dispatch remains disabled until durable replay/request infrastructure and membership-generation revalidation exist.
evidence_note: Grounded in job_node_allocator_v0.6-network6 and rexxos_managed_compute_mu_v0.1-dev2 Library deliveries inspected 2026-10-23.
